title: IoU, NMS & mAP for Detection
interviewAnswer: Intersection-over-Union measures box overlap; Non-Maximum Suppression removes redundant overlapping predictions; mAP summarizes precision-recall across classes and IoU thresholds depending on benchmark.
keyPoints: IoU threshold defines a localization match.
NMS threshold affects duplicate vs missed close objects.
why: IoU, NMS & mAP for Detection is a standard part of a broad data/ML curriculum because it changes how models are selected, evaluated or operated in real systems.
intuition: IoU threshold defines a localization match.
deepDive: Intersection-over-Union measures box overlap; Non-Maximum Suppression removes redundant overlapping predictions; mAP summarizes precision-recall across classes and IoU thresholds depending on benchmark. NMS threshold affects duplicate vs missed close objects. mAP hides per-class/size performance. A strong answer connects the formal idea to validation, data requirements and failure modes instead of treating the method as a recipe.
workedExample: A predicted box with IoU 0.8 can count as a true localization while multiple overlapping boxes may need NMS.
commonMistakes: Choosing the technique without checking whether its assumptions match the problem.
Optimizing an offline metric without checking realistic validation slices or operational constraints.
followUps: When would you not use IoU, NMS & mAP for Detection?
How would you validate or tune IoU, NMS & mAP for Detection?
production: In production, validate on realistic slices, track latency/cost when relevant, and monitor for distribution changes or failure modes that the offline metric can hide.
